transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I used to be able to focus for hours on designs, but now my mind feels foggy and I can’t make even basic decisions at work. It's a huge change from how I used to be, and I'm just really struggling to get through my tasks.
Have you experienced any major life changes or stressful events recently around the time these difficulties started?

About fourteen months ago, I transitioned from an internship into a demanding, full-time engineering technician role on a high-visibility aerospace project with tight deadlines and a strict supervisor. I tried to cope at first by working late nights and weekends to keep up, but the constant stress and heavy workload eventually wore me down. I think that's what triggered these major issues with my focus and decision-making.
Along with the difficulty focusing, have you been feeling persistently down or lost interest in activities you normally enjoy?

Yes, I've been feeling really down, and the things I used to love just feel completely flat and pointless now. I used to get excited about tinkering with 3-D printers or going on long runs with my track club, but now I just end up sitting on my couch scrolling through old emails instead.
How long have you been feeling this down and lacking interest in your hobbies, and has this been happening nearly every day?

Yes, I've felt this way nearly every single day for a little over a year now, starting not long after I transitioned to the full-time position. For months, hobbies like running with my track club or tinkering with 3-D printers have just felt completely flat and pointless.
Besides feeling down, have you also been experiencing constant, excessive worry or anxiety about work or other areas of your life that you find hard to control?

Yes, I'm constantly consumed by this intense worry about work that I just can't seem to control. I lie awake at night replaying every tiny mistake, terrified that I've ruined the entire project. I've even become convinced that my boss is secretly gathering evidence to hold me personally responsible when something goes wrong.
You mentioned intense worry about work. Do you also find yourself constantly worrying about other areas of your life, like your health, family, finances, or even minor daily matters?

No, not really. My mind is almost entirely consumed by my work, the mistakes I've made, and the fear of being held responsible for them. I don't really have the mental space to worry about my health, family, or finances right now.
Along with feeling down, have you been experiencing a significant loss of energy or feeling constantly exhausted, even without physical exertion?

Yes, I feel completely exhausted all the time, even though I'm not doing heavy physical labor. My body constantly feels like it's moving through molasses, and I'm usually too drained to handle social plans or function normally outside of work.
When you are feeling this low, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or felt that life is no longer worth living?

On bad nights when I feel overwhelmed by guilt, I catch myself wishing I just wouldn’t wake up. I've even had detailed thoughts about driving my car off the overpass on my commute. I haven't acted on any of those thoughts, but they are really scary.
Have you ever experienced a similar period of feeling very down, exhausted, and losing interest in your hobbies before this current episode started a year ago?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like this before. This is the very first time I’ve ever felt this way, and it’s completely different from how I used to be. Before this past year, I was always able to handle my work and enjoy my life.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight since these feelings started, such as eating much less or more than usual?

I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my appetite or weight. However, actually deciding what to eat for dinner has become a huge struggle that can paralyze me for fifteen minutes. My mind just feels too foggy to make even simple choices like that.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns since this started, such as having trouble falling asleep, waking up in the middle of the night, or sleeping much more than usual?
I haven't really tracked my sleep patterns specifically. Other than lying awake some nights worrying about work, I'm not really sure if there's been a big change.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt the opposite of this—with extremely high energy, needing very little sleep, or feeling unusually happy and 'on top of the world'?

No, I've never experienced anything like that. Even on my rare better days, my energy and mood only ever get closer to a baseline normal, never elevated or unusually high. I have definitely never felt 'on top of the world.'
Do you have any underlying medical conditions, or do you use alcohol, medications, or other substances? I want to make sure we rule out any physical causes for how you've been feeling.
No, I don't have any known underlying medical conditions. I also don't really drink alcohol, take any medications, or use any other substances.

He presents with a first-time onset of severe depressive symptoms lasting over a year, triggered by a stressful work transition. He exhibits at least six key depressive symptoms: persistent depressed mood, marked anhedonia, profound fatigue, cognitive difficulties (foggy thinking and severe indecisiveness), excessive guilt/paranoia regarding work performance, and active suicidal ideation with a specific plan (driving off an overpass).
